[Starbucks](https://www.starbucks.com/) has rehired Anomaly and artist Geoff McFetridge for a second straight holiday campaign.

The 2026 spot, "**Perfect Harmony**," is a 30-second animation that McFetridge drew by hand on Starbucks cups using a Sharpie.

Rehiring the same team gives the brand a holiday look that customers can now recognize two years running.

In a separate effort, Starbucks released "Holiday Blend," a seven-track album through [Interscope Records](https://interscope.com/) and [Universal Music Group](https://www.universalmusic.com/).

[//www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/nHPorplY6ng](https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/nHPorplY6ng)

The projects give Starbucks **two ways to reach customers during the holiday season**.

And for [Anomaly](https://www.designrush.com/agency/profile/anomaly-partners), the holiday film adds to its Starbucks relationship.

The agency has handled the brand's U.S. creative account since January 2025, after WPP held the business for about three months.

Anomaly's first Starbucks spot, "[Not My Name](https://news.designrush.com/anomaly-debuts-not-my-name-its-first-ever-campaign-as-starbucks-new-aor)," also focused on the handwritten names and notes baristas put on cups, a ritual unique to the chain.

After two agency changes in three months, Starbucks steadied its [brand positioning](https://www.designrush.com/agency/logo-branding/trends/brand-positioning) by keeping its creative work anchored to one in-store ritual.

## Two Music Labels Back the Holiday Album

"**Holiday Blend**" features Magnus Ferrell, Coco Jones, JYT, TRÍADA, Brandi Carlile, The Womack Sisters, and Leon Thomas.

The seven tracks include **reinterpretations of holiday classics** and **an original song by JYT**.

Thursday, Oct. 29, 2026

- **Consolidated Net Revenue** -- $9.1 billion in Q4, representing a 3.9% decrease on a constant currency basis due to the transition of China retail operations to a licensed joint venture model.
- **Global Comparable Coffeehouse Sales** -- 7.2% growth in Q4, driven by a 5.2% increase in average ticket and a 1.8% increase in comparable transactions.
- **U.S. Comparable Coffeehouse Sales** -- 7.7% growth in Q4, reflecting a 5.2% ticket increase and a 2.4% transaction increase with growth across all dayparts and income levels.
- **North America Comparable Coffeehouse Sales** -- 7.9% growth in Q4, supported by double-digit comparable growth in Canada.
- **Non-GAAP Consolidated Operating Margin** -- 14% in Q4, an expansion of 450 basis points year over year driven by sales leverage, disciplined execution, and cost savings.
- **Non-GAAP EPS** -- $0.80 in Q4, representing 54% growth year over year and exceeding the high end of previous guidance.
- **Full-Year Fiscal 2026 Revenue** -- $37.9 billion, a 2.1% increase compared to the prior year.
- **Full-Year Non-GAAP EPS** -- $2.72, representing 27% growth year over year.
- **Starbucks Rewards Membership** -- 36 million 90-day active members in the U.S., a record high representing sequential and year-over-year growth.
- **Global Coffeehouse Count** -- 41,607 locations at fiscal year-end, following 617 net new openings during the year.
- **North America Store Portfolio Actions** -- 250 company-operated coffeehouse closures completed in Sept. 2026 as part of a portfolio optimization strategy.
- **Uplift Program** -- 1,700 total coffeehouse renovations completed across North America by fiscal year-end, with plans for more than 2,000 additional uplifts in fiscal 2027.
- **Fiscal 2027 Revenue Guidance** -- A projected 1% decrease in consolidated net revenues, including approximately $700 million in revenue from a 53rd week.
- **Fiscal 2027 Comparable Sales Guidance** -- Approximately 4% growth in North America comparable coffeehouse sales.
- **Fiscal 2027 Operating Margin Guidance** -- 13.5% to 14.0%, representing a midpoint expansion of 190 basis points.
- **Fiscal 2027 Non-GAAP EPS Guidance** -- $3.15 to $3.25, which includes a benefit of more than $0.10 from the 53rd week.
- **Fiscal 2027 Net New Openings Guidance** -- Approximately 1,200 net new coffeehouses globally, with 1,100 in International markets and 90 to 100 in North America.
- **Cost Savings Program** -- Management reported achieving more than 50% of its $2 billion gross savings goal, with further cost of goods sold benefits expected through fiscal 2028.

# Toulouse brew up official partnership with US brand Starbucks

3rd September 2026

![](https://www.insideworldfootball.com/app/uploads/2026/09/Starbucks-e1788432530722.jpg)

September 3 – Starbucks will put its logo on a football shirt for the first time after signing a partnership with Ligue 1 club Toulouse for the 2026/27 season. 

The US coffee chain became an Official Partner of Toulouse this morning, with its Siren logo taking the sleeve position on the men’s first-team shirt as well as the club’s academy kits. Despite that significance, no financial details have been officially disclosed. 

The agreement was brokered by Sportfive alongside Jaune, Starbucks’ creative agency in France, and will also cover the usual roster of matchday activations at Stadium de Toulouse, digital content and supporter experiences – which are to be expected with this type of deal. 

This move represents another step into major sport for Starbucks, after it became Official Coffee Partner of the LA28 Olympic and Paralympic Games and Team USA last year. 

Toulouse President Olivier Cloarec said: “We are extremely proud to partner with Starbucks. It is an iconic, globally recognised brand, and its decision to partner with our club and align with our identity is a tremendous acknowledgment of TéFéCé’s growing appeal and reach.  

“This also marks a first for Starbucks – appearing on a football club’s jersey for the very first time – which makes the partnership even more special for us. We are delighted to write this new chapter together and share the journey with our community.” 

Anaïs Dezoteux, Marketing Director at Starbucks France, said: “Coffee has always been at the heart of Starbucks, driven by the belief that a single cup can create a genuine moment of connection.  

“This experience comes to life every day in our stores, thanks to our baristas who create these shared moments with our customers. With TéFéCé, we want to go even further by envisioning new ways to bring the coffee and Starbucks experience to life within the unifying world of football.  

“This partnership offers a fantastic opportunity for innovation and creativity – allowing us to take the experience beyond our stores, create unique encounters, and – together with our baristas and the fans – imagine new ways to connect over coffee.” 

Sportfive Managing Director Xavier Oddone added: “The arrival of Starbucks alongside Toulouse FC is a powerful illustration of the evolution of sports marketing: brands today are seeking platforms capable of forging genuine connections with fans. This historic first for Starbucks in football demonstrates TéFéCé’s strong appeal, and we are delighted to have helped bring this major partnership to life.”

The Starbucks Bearista Christmas takeover at CapitaLand malls is on now, and the Raffles City pop-up closes on 22 November, so this weekend is your last chance to see it there. The campaign runs from 11 November to 31 December 2026 across 16 CapitaLand malls, with giant Bearista figures, a travelling pop-up, a mall-exclusive drink at S$8.60 and eCapitaVoucher rewards of up to S$15 on weekday spending.

CapitaLand says it is Singapore’s largest Starbucks holiday takeover, and it ties in with Starbucks’ 30th year in Singapore. Here is what to expect and how to pick up the freebies.

## Where to see the Starbucks Bearista displays

Five Bearistas, named Dasha, Jam, Brewster, Snowmallow and Star, appear as oversized displays in the participating malls. They are set up for photos, and CapitaLand lists the exact spots below.

- Raffles City Singapore: Christmas tree Bearista at the L1 external quartzite, near North Bridge Road
- Bugis Junction: L1 Fountain Square
- Plaza Singapura: L1 near Starbucks, the outdoor space near the entrance and the lift lobby near MUJI
- Funan: the Atrium and the L1 North Bridge Road entrance
- Other malls: Aperia Mall, Bedok Mall, Bugis+, CQ @ Clarke Quay, IMM Building, Junction 8, Kallang Wave Mall, Lot One, Sengkang Grand Mall, SingPost Centre, Tampines Mall and Westgate

![Starbucks Bearista Christmas inflatable at Bugis Junction](https://littlebigreddot.com/wp-content/uploads/bugisj.jpg)

*Source: CapitaLand*

If you like a photo contest, CapitaLand is running one until 11 December. Snap yourself with a Bearista inflatable, follow @CapitaLandMallsSG, @StarbucksSG and @CapitaStarSG, tag a friend and post to a public account. Eight winners get a Starbucks 12oz ceramic mug with a Bearista plush.

## Starbucks Bearista Christmas pop-up at Raffles City and Bugis+

The main attraction is The Bearista Holiday Experience, a travelling pop-up that is open daily from 10am to 10pm. It is at the Raffles City L3 Atrium until 22 November, then moves to the Bugis+ L2 Atrium from 25 November to 6 December.

It includes Starbucks Singapore’s first Create-Your-Own Cold Foam Beverage Bar, a Bearista plushie wall and a personality quiz that matches you with one of the five Bearistas. A cup-built installation marks Starbucks’ 30 years in Singapore.

Key in the reward code BEARISTA on the CapitaStar app to unlock the pop-up experiences. The Raffles City leg has a local twist, a Kaya Toast Cold Foam with Buttery Croutons that is sold only there. At Bugis+, the exclusive is a Chocolate Chip Cookie cold foam.

![Starbucks Bearista Christmas display at Plaza Singapura](https://littlebigreddot.com/wp-content/uploads/plaza.jpg)

*Source: CapitaLand*

## Merchandise, workshops and the S$8.60 latte

Starbucks Rewards members get 10 per cent off Starbucks merchandise with a minimum spend of S$80 at the pop-up. Every merchandise purchase also comes with a Buy-1-Get-1-Free Venti beverage voucher, valid at nine participating Starbucks stores in CapitaLand malls. Spend S$100 at the pop-up and you can redeem an event-exclusive Bearista pin set.

Coffee and craft workshops are for two people each and run on a first-come, first-served basis. Raffles City sessions are on 14 to 22 November (Monday to Friday at 7pm, weekends at 11am, 2pm and 5pm), and the Bugis+ sessions were listed as fully booked at the time of writing. Spending a minimum of S$60 at the pop-up is the route to a workshop place.

The drink to look out for is the Iced Hazelnut Bianco Latte, a mall-exclusive at participating Starbucks stores in CapitaLand malls from 11 November to 31 December. A grande is S$8.60. If you are after the rest of the seasonal drinks, see our guide to the [Starbucks Singapore Christmas 2026 menu](https://littlebigreddot.com/starbucks-singapore-christmas-2026-toffee-nut-crunch-peppermint-mocha/).

## How to earn eCapitaVouchers from your Christmas shopping

On weekdays from 11 November to 24 December, shoppers can earn up to S$25 in eCapitaVouchers with a minimum spend at participating malls. The tiers depend on the mall, and each needs a linked payment method or eCapitaVoucher on your CapitaStar account.

- S$60 spend for S$5: Aperia Mall, Kallang Wave Mall, Sengkang Grand Mall
- S$120 spend for S$10: SingPost Centre
- S$150 spend for S$12: Bedok Mall, Bugis+, CQ @ Clarke Quay, Lot One
- S$180 spend for S$15: Bugis Junction, Funan, IMM Building, Junction 8, Plaza Singapura and The Atrium @ Orchard, Tampines Mall, Westgate

Redemptions are capped daily per mall (70 to 150 depending on the mall), limited to one per member per day per mall, and same-day combined transactions must include at least S$20 per receipt. Tiers above S$60 also need one receipt of at least S$50. Supermarkets are excluded except for a few named ones. DBS/POSB users linked to CapitaStar can also get S$10 for a single S$250 transaction, for the first 13,500 redemptions, released in weekly tranches of 2,250 on Wednesdays until 16 December.

Separately, the CapitaStar app has a Bearista stamp card. Complete activities worth 30 stamps by 31 December and you can exchange them for a surprise reward, ranging from up to 100,000 STAR$ (worth S$100) to merchandise such as a Bearista cushion or a stainless steel Christmas tumbler.

## Plan your visit

Weekday visits also line up with the eCapitaVoucher tiers above, and the 7pm workshop slots suit an after-work stop. Raffles City is a short walk from City Hall MRT (EW13/NS25), and Bugis+ connects to Bugis MRT (EW12/DT14). Terms apply and stock is limited. Check the CapitaStar app and capitaland.com for the latest mechanics, as vouchers and merchandise run out daily.

This year, Dunkin' is wrapping cups, donut boxes and Munchkins boxes with a colorful "Donutcracker" design that "reimagines the classic holiday nutcracker with donut-inspired details, festive sprinkles and the brand's signature pink-and-orange flair," [according](https://news.dunkindonuts.com/news/dunkin-holiday-menu-november-2026) to the coffee chain.

![PHOTO: Starbucks and Dunkin are launching their 2026 holiday menus and items this November.](https://i.abcnewsfe.com/a/01a0c394-35cc-4f36-8bb9-436c46df45c7/coffee-ht-er-261104_1793813281710_hpMain_4x3.jpg)

Starbucks and Dunkin' are launching their 2026 holiday menus and items this November.

Returning holiday beverages -- all of which are available now -- include [Cookie Butter](https://www.goodmorningamerica.com/food/story/new-holiday-coca-cola-flavor-creamy-vanilla-127016496) coffees, lattes, hot chocolates, and matchas, as well as Toasted White Chocolate lattes, the Almond White Chocolate Shakin' Espresso, and the​ Raspberry White Chocolate Matcha with Toasted White Chocolate swirl.

Starbucks' holiday menu items and new products debuted Nov. 5, with the chain's iconic holiday cups all dressed up in bows, garlands and trees. A special holiday-themed 3.5-ounce pup cup design joins the lineup this season as well, featuring an adorable dog illustration inspired by a "real-life beagle named Junie," [according](https://about.starbucks.com/stories/2026/starbucks-2026-holiday-cups-the-story-behind-the-ribbons-retro-colors-and-first-ever-holiday-pup-cup/) to Starbucks.

# Starbucks announces new growth strategy in Brazil

Posted 16 November, 2026

[Share on Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https://www.teaandcoffee.net/news/40523/starbucks-announces-new-growth-strategy-in-brazil/) Share on LinkedIn [Share on X](https://x.com/intent/post?text=https://www.teaandcoffee.net/news/40523/starbucks-announces-new-growth-strategy-in-brazil/)

Image credit: Starbucks

Together with its licensed partner [ZAMP](http://zamp.com.br), [Starbucks](http://www.starbucks.com) reinforced Brazil’s role as a strategic market for long-term growth in Latin America and the Caribbean.

Following a period focused on strengthening its foundation and reconnecting with customers, Starbucks is entering a new chapter of growth in Brazil, expanding into new cities, strengthening its presence in key existing markets, and exploring new coffeehouse formats and experiences.

By the end of 2026, the Seattle, Washington-based coffeehouse chain expects to open approximately 10 new coffeehouses across São Paulo, Belo Horizonte and Fortaleza. The expansion will mark Starbucks first entry into Ceará and extend its presence into Brazil’s Northeast, bringing the ‘Starbucks Experience’ to Fortaleza, one of the region’s leading tourism destinations, with plans for two coffeehouses at Fortaleza Airport and another location in the city center at Shopping Iguatemi Bosque.

Starbucks growth in Brazil is guided by customer demand, cultural relevance and long-term operational excellence. Rather than growth for growth’s sake, the company is focused on expanding its presence thoughtfully while creating experiences that reflect how customers across Brazil enjoy coffee and connect with one another.

That strategy also includes exploring new coffeehouse formats and customer occasions. In 2027, Starbucks plans to open two coffeehouse locations at Beto Carrero World – including one in the park’s Cowboyland district – expanding the brand into one of Brazil’s leading entertainment destinations and creating new ways for customers to experience Starbucks beyond its traditional coffeehouse settings.

At the same time, Starbucks is beginning to bring its evolved coffeehouse experience to Brazil, with refreshed spaces designed to feel warmer and more welcoming while celebrating coffee craft, human connection and community.

“Our connection to Brazil is longstanding, rooted in the coffee we have proudly sourced here for decades and the relationships we have built with customers over the years. Together with ZAMP, we are building on that foundation through thoughtful, purpose-driven growth focused on creating the right coffeehouse experiences in the right places while continuing to invest in coffee and the connections we create in communities across Brazil,” said Ricardo Arias-Nath, Starbucks svp of global coffee & tea and president of Latin America and the Caribbean.

As Starbucks grows, the company continues to evolve its experience around Brazilian tastes, routines and coffee culture.

Recent innovations such as [Cafézinho Brasileiro](https://historias.starbucks.com/br/press/2025/starbucks-celebra-o-jeito-brasileiro-de-tomar-cafe-com-novos-formatos-no-cardapio-nacional/) reflect this approach, drawing inspiration from Brazil’s deep coffee traditions while delivering an experience distinctly Starbucks. Longtime favourites including pão de queijo, Brigadeiro Frappuccino® Blended Beverage and Panettone, as well as locally developed beverage platforms such as Média Pingado, demonstrate how Starbucks continues to build stronger connections with Brazilian customers through products and experiences created with local relevance in mind.

This holiday season, Starbucks will continue that tradition with its holiday beverage lineup and the return of the beloved Panettone dessert, bringing familiar seasonal rituals to coffeehouses across the market.

“As we look to the future of Starbucks in Brazil, we are listening to our customers and continuing to evolve the customer experience in ways that feel relevant to how Brazilians enjoy coffee and connect every day. We also remain grounded in what has always made Starbucks special: our passion for coffee, the connection our partners create, and the welcoming coffeehouse experience customers know and love,” said Mariane Wiederkehr, managing director of Starbucks Brazil.
